Package index

Setting up

The engine is Python, installed on first use. These three say where it is, what it found, and which build of PyTorch to ask for.

platypus_status()
Is the engine ready?
platypus_device()
Where the work will happen
platypus_use_torch()
Ask for a particular PyTorch build

A specification

One object says what to train, on what data, with what. Built from arguments or from YAML - the same specification either way.

platypus_spec()
Build an experiment specification
segmentation_data()
Where the images and masks are
detection_data()
Where the images and their annotation files are
u_net() u_net_plus_plus() res_u_net() linknet()
Segmentation models
yolo3()
YOLOv3
as.list(<platypus_spec>)
Turn a specification back into plain R data

Losses, metrics, optimisers, callbacks, augmentation, encoders.

The data on disk

Splitting by patient rather than by slice, and looking at what is actually there before spending an afternoon training on it.

platypus_split()
Split a dataset into training, validation and test sets
split_files()
The files in one part of a split
read_images()
Read images as the model sees them
read_masks()
Read mask files as class indices
volume_info()
What is in a volume file
series_report()
Check folders of DICOM slices before training on them
mask_report()
What the colormap or labels match in your masks

Predicting and scoring

evaluate()
Compare the trained models

Score every case separately

evaluate_images()

detection_crops()

Looking at the results

A figure is the point. These are the ones you put in a paper.

plot_masks()
Look at masks beside the images they came from
plot_boxes()
Draw boxes on images
plot_anchors()
Draw the anchors against the boxes they were fitted to
overlay_mask()
Lay a mask over the image it belongs to
overlay_agreement()
Where a prediction and the truth disagree
